diagnostic_approaches.name: Bronchoscopy (direct visualization)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Evaluate presence, degree, and extent of airway stenosis; assist in establishing underlying etiology
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Direct visualization via bronchoscopy; both flexible and rigid approaches apply.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Best method for evaluating airway stenosis
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: the best method for evaluating the presence, degree, and extent of an airway stenosis is direct visualization via bronchoscopy.

diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Assist diagnosis of airway stenosis as an ancillary study
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Better than standard radiographs or tomograms
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Ancillary study to assist evaluation when stenosis suspected
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: ancillary studies such as imaging (CT with reconstruction better than standard radiographs or tomograms), flow volume loops, and clinical exam.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Clinical exam (focal wheeze)
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Patients may have a focal wheeze on exam
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When evaluating patients presenting with dyspnea
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Patients typically present with dyspnea and may have a focal wheeze on exam.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Symptom recurrence assessment
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify recurrent airway stenosis after prior treatment
criteria_or_scoring: Return of initial symptoms may indicate recurrence
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Return of initial symptoms may be a sign of recurrent stenosis
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: In patients with prior treatment for airway stenosis
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Return of initial symptoms, which may be slowly progressive in some instances, may be a sign of recurrent stenosis in those with prior treatment.

definitions.content: A nonconformal balloon is one that dilates to the desired conﬁguration and diameter without molding to the shape of the stenosis.
definitions.source_excerpt: A nonconformal balloon is one that dilates to the desired conﬁguration and diameter without molding to the shape of the stenosis.

clinical_pearls.content: A simple, safe, direct, inexpensive, repeatable, and rapidly effective option is balloon dilation, also called balloon bronchoplasty.

technology_and_technique.summary: Direct visualization via bronchoscopy is stated as the best method to assess presence, degree, and extent of airway stenosis. Both flexible and rigid bronchoscopy are applicable and may also be therapeutic. No specific diagnostic yield percentages or safety rates are provided.
technology_and_technique.reference: Kovitz KL, Yong SS. Balloon Dilation Techniques. In: Principles and Practice of Interventional Pulmonology. Springer; 2025. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_35-1

technology_and_technique.topic: Imaging comparison: CT with reconstruction vs standard radiographs/tomograms
technology_and_technique.summary: CT with reconstruction is described as better than standard radiographs or tomograms for ancillary evaluation of suspected airway stenosis. No sensitivity/specificity or yield statistics are reported.
technology_and_technique.reference: Kovitz KL, Yong SS. Balloon Dilation Techniques. In: Principles and Practice of Interventional Pulmonology. Springer; 2025. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_35-1

technology_and_technique.summary: Flow-volume loops can assist in raising suspicion for airway stenosis but are adjunctive; definitive evaluation relies on bronchoscopy. No performance metrics are provided.
technology_and_technique.reference: Kovitz KL, Yong SS. Balloon Dilation Techniques. In: Principles and Practice of Interventional Pulmonology. Springer; 2025. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_35-1

technology_and_technique.topic: Patient selection cues for stenosis evaluation
technology_and_technique.summary: Typical features include dyspnea and focal wheeze; patients are often misdiagnosed with asthma. Recurrence of initial symptoms can indicate restenosis after prior treatment. A high index of suspicion is recommended, prompting imaging and bronchoscopy.
technology_and_technique.reference: Kovitz KL, Yong SS. Balloon Dilation Techniques. In: Principles and Practice of Interventional Pulmonology. Springer; 2025. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_35-1

technology_and_technique.topic: Flexible vs rigid bronchoscopy: selection factors
technology_and_technique.summary: Both flexible and rigid approaches are suitable for evaluation and therapy. Selection depends on planned intervention, operator/institution experience, and airway stability requirements. No comparative effectiveness or outcome statistics are provided.
technology_and_technique.reference: Kovitz KL, Yong SS. Balloon Dilation Techniques. In: Principles and Practice of Interventional Pulmonology. Springer; 2025. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_35-1

technology_and_technique.summary: Patients typically need an established airway (laryngeal mask airway, endotracheal tube, or rigid bronchoscope). Choice is driven by stenosis location, experience, and planned intervention. Deep sedation/anesthesia is generally required (except possibly very distal stenoses); anesthesia support is preferred.
technology_and_technique.reference: Kovitz KL, Yong SS. Balloon Dilation Techniques. In: Principles and Practice of Interventional Pulmonology. Springer; 2025. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_35-1

technology_and_technique.summary: Use nonconformal balloons long enough to straddle the stenosis with about 1 cm overlap on each side. Begin with a smaller diameter and perform serial dilations; the largest balloon should be several millimeters larger than the desired final airway diameter. Use an inflation device with pressure gauge. Some balloons pass through flexible bronchoscope channels; others require a larger channel or over-the-wire placement. Avoid wire-only placement/dilation without bronchoscopic guidance.
technology_and_technique.reference: Kovitz KL, Yong SS. Balloon Dilation Techniques. In: Principles and Practice of Interventional Pulmonology. Springer; 2025. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_35-1

technology_and_technique.topic: Technology comparison: airway-specific vs GI/vascular balloons
technology_and_technique.summary: Airway-specific, gastroenterologic, and vascular balloons are all used. GI/bronchoscopic balloons are often less expensive than vascular balloons. Functional considerations include compatibility with bronchoscope working channels and availability of radiopaque markers. No comparative efficacy or safety data are provided.
technology_and_technique.reference: Kovitz KL, Yong SS. Balloon Dilation Techniques. In: Principles and Practice of Interventional Pulmonology. Springer; 2025. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_35-1

technology_and_technique.topic: Role of balloon dilation in multimodality care
technology_and_technique.summary: Balloon bronchoplasty can be stand-alone or combined with stenting, laser, other thermal therapies, or local medications. Balloons can aid stent deployment/seating and may temporize to allow progression to more invasive techniques.
technology_and_technique.reference: Kovitz KL, Yong SS. Balloon Dilation Techniques. In: Principles and Practice of Interventional Pulmonology. Springer; 2025. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_35-1

technology_and_technique.topic: Safety and effectiveness of balloon bronchoplasty
technology_and_technique.summary: Characterized as simple, safe, inexpensive, repeatable, and rapidly effective with potential for immediate symptomatic improvement. The chapter does not report specific complication rates, diagnostic yields, or comparative effectiveness statistics.
technology_and_technique.reference: Kovitz KL, Yong SS. Balloon Dilation Techniques. In: Principles and Practice of Interventional Pulmonology. Springer; 2025. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_35-1

technology_and_technique.summary: No randomized or head-to-head clinical trial data comparing bronchoscopy approaches, imaging strategies, or balloon types are presented in this chapter.
technology_and_technique.reference: Kovitz KL, Yong SS. Balloon Dilation Techniques. In: Principles and Practice of Interventional Pulmonology. Springer; 2025. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_35-1
